dialogue.content: こんばんは
dialogue.English: Good evening.

dialogue.content: こんばんは、よろしくおねがいいたします。年齢、性別、ご相談内容を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Good evening. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.content: はい。16歳女です学校がつらいです
dialogue.English: Yes. I'm a 16-year-old girl. I'm having a hard time at school.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。それはとてもお辛いですね。答えられる範囲で構いません。どうかされましたか？
dialogue.English: I see. That must be very difficult for you. Please share only what you feel comfortable with. Could you tell me what's been happening?

dialogue.content: クラスに馴染めません。
dialogue.English: I can't seem to fit in with my class.

dialogue.content: 自分は嫌われてるかもしれないと思います。
dialogue.English: I feel like I might be disliked.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。どうしてそう思われたんですか？
dialogue.English: I see. What makes you feel that way?

dialogue.content: クラスメートはみんなフレンドリーで、名前を呼び捨てしてって言われるけど、中学からの癖でなかなか呼べません。そう言われると戸惑ってうまく言葉が出てこなくて、
dialogue.English: All my classmates are friendly, and they tell me to call them by their first names, but it's a habit from middle school that I just can't break. When they say that, I get flustered and can't find the right words,

dialogue.content: 黙ってしまうので、みんな私を変な人だと思ってると思います
dialogue.English: and I end up going quiet, so I think everyone sees me as weird.

dialogue.content: なかなか直ぐには呼び捨てで呼べないですよね。
dialogue.English: It's not easy to switch to calling people by their first names right away, is it?

dialogue.content: はい。でもみんな呼び捨てしてます。あと、自分も呼び捨てされてます。
dialogue.English: Yes. But everyone else calls each other by their first names. And they call me by my first name too.

dialogue.content: 戸惑う気持ちが分かります。
dialogue.English: I can understand why you'd feel flustered.

dialogue.content: うまく呼び捨てに慣れてないと言いたいけど、言えなくて
dialogue.English: I want to tell them I'm just not used to calling people by their first names, but I can't bring myself to say it.

dialogue.content: そんな自分も嫌だなと思います
dialogue.English: And I dislike myself for being like that.

dialogue.content: あら、名前を呼ばれているんですね。なかなか慣れていないと違和感があるのかしら？
dialogue.English: Oh, so they're calling you by your first name too. Does it feel strange since you're not used to it?

dialogue.content: 自分がそう呼ばれるのは特に違和感ないです
dialogue.English: It doesn't feel particularly strange when they call me that.

dialogue.content: みんな陽キャだから
dialogue.English: It's because they're all outgoing people.

dialogue.content: お友達この事も呼び捨てにしたいですか？
dialogue.English: Do you want to call your friends by their first names too?

dialogue.content: 私は元々ひとりでいるのが好き
dialogue.English: I'm someone who basically likes being by myself.

dialogue.content: 友達は5人いて、さん付けです。
dialogue.English: I have five friends, and I use "-san" with their names.

dialogue.content: 距離感を持ってると思われるかも
dialogue.English: They might think I'm keeping my distance.

dialogue.content: 陰キャのクラスメイトさんもいるんではないですか
dialogue.English: Aren't there any introverted classmates as well?

dialogue.content: 休み時間もみんな自分のとこに集まってくるので、疲れてしまうことがあります
dialogue.English: During break time, everyone gathers around me, which can be tiring sometimes.

dialogue.content: たまに疲れてひとりになりたいなと思います
dialogue.English: Sometimes I get tired and just want to be alone.

dialogue.content: でも友達にも悪くて言えないです
dialogue.English: But I feel bad and can't say that to my friends.

dialogue.content: みんなのようにできないから、きっと嫌われてます
dialogue.English: I can't be like everyone else, so I'm sure they dislike me.

dialogue.content: ひとりで居たいのだけどみんなよってきてしまうんですね。人気があるんですね。でもひとりで居たいのですか
dialogue.English: So you want to be alone, but everyone comes to you. It sounds like you're popular. But you'd rather be alone?

dialogue.content: 嫌われていたら相談者様のところへ集まらないのでは？
dialogue.English: If you were disliked, they wouldn't gather around you, would they?

dialogue.content: ひとりでいたいと思うことはおかしいですか
dialogue.English: Is it strange to want to be alone?

dialogue.content: 全然、おかしくないとおもいますよ。誰でも思うことだと。
dialogue.English: Not at all. I think everyone feels that way at times.

dialogue.content: 相談者様、陽キャではないんですか？
dialogue.English: Would you say you're not the outgoing type?

dialogue.content: お話ししずらいですか？
dialogue.English: Is it hard for you to talk about this?

dialogue.content: 違います。なるべく目立ちたくない
dialogue.English: No, I'm not. I prefer not to stand out.

dialogue.content: ノリも悪くて
dialogue.English: And I'm not good at going along with the vibe.

dialogue.content: みんな扱いづらいかもしれません
dialogue.English: They might find me hard to deal with.

dialogue.content: そんな自分でもどうやったらクラスで楽に自分らしく過ごせるか
dialogue.English: Even for someone like me, how can I be myself and feel more at ease in class?

dialogue.content: どうすればいいでしょうか
dialogue.English: What should I do?

dialogue.content: そうなんですか。相談者様は人気者の様に感じました。でもなるべく静かに過ごしたいんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. I got the impression that you were very popular. But you'd prefer to spend your time quietly.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: では、一緒に考えましょう。
dialogue.English: Then let's think it through together.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 何が一番辛いですか
dialogue.English: What is the most difficult part for you?

dialogue.content: んー、名前の呼び方？
dialogue.English: Hmm... is it the way you address names?

dialogue.content: ひとりになる時間がないことと、クラスメートに何か言われたときに言葉に詰まってしまう事です。意識しないで自分らしく過ごせるかです
dialogue.English: Not having any time to myself, and getting tongue-tied when classmates say something to me. And it's about whether I can be myself without being self-conscious.

dialogue.content: 自分らしくってどんな感じなのか教えてもらえます学校の中でひとりになりたいのですか
dialogue.English: Could you tell me what 'being yourself' feels like to you? Do you want to be alone at school?

dialogue.content: ひとりになりたいし、のんびりしたいのですかね。
dialogue.English: You want to be alone and take it easy, perhaps?

dialogue.content: 言葉に詰まらないで、呼び捨て苦手って言いたいし、たまに図書館等で一人になれるかなって思います
dialogue.English: I'd like to be able to say I'm not comfortable calling people by their first names without getting tongue-tied, and to sometimes have time alone in a place like the library.

dialogue.content: のんびりしたいかもしれません
dialogue.English: I might want to take it easy.

dialogue.content: ずっと今まで我慢して学校に通っていたんですね。ひとりでも打ち明けられるとよいですね。
dialogue.English: You've been enduring this all this time at school. It would be good if you could open up to even one person.

dialogue.content: は
dialogue.English: Oh.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 学校以外はのんびりできてますか？
dialogue.English: Are you able to relax outside of school?

dialogue.content: 家ではのんびりできるので早く帰りたいって思います
dialogue.English: I can relax at home, so I want to go home early.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 学校で無理をして生活しているのですね。つらいですね、、、
dialogue.English: So you're forcing yourself to get through the day at school. That must be tough...

dialogue.content: 食事取れてますか
dialogue.English: Are you able to eat properly?

dialogue.content: ちゃんと食べてます。
dialogue.English: I'm eating properly.

dialogue.content: よかったです。
dialogue.English: That's good to hear.

dialogue.content: たまにひとりになりたいときは図書館に行こうと思います。あと、まだ2ヶ月なのでもう少し慣れてきたらクラスメートに言えるといいなと思いました
dialogue.English: When I want to be alone sometimes, I think I'll try going to the library. Also, it's only been two months, so I hope that as I get more used to things, I'll be able to tell my classmates.

dialogue.content: それはとてもよかったです。これから笑い顔が見られることを楽しみにしています。また、ご相談にいらしてくださいね。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: That's wonderful to hear. I look forward to seeing you smile more in the future. Please feel free to come and talk anytime. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: (大変、勉強になりました。ありがとうございました。)
dialogue.English: (This has been a great learning experience. Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそ拙い相談者でした。ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Likewise. I was a rather inarticulate client; thank you.)

dialogue.content: (それでは、また評価よろしくお願いいたします。失礼いたします。ありがとうございました。)
dialogue.English: (Well then, I look forward to your evaluation. Goodbye. Thank you.)
